## Your right to convert to a permanent life insurance policy

At any time, up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the health of the insured person , you may convert the insurance in effect under this policy . The converted insurance will be for an amount not to exceed the Sum Insured (provided on the Policy Schedule) and will be on any permanent plan we make available for such conversion.

To exercise the conversion option, you must complete an application form which we will provide and pay us the first premium required for the converted insurance. Contingent Beneficiary Designation: A 'secondary' list of beneficiary(ies) , (subrogated in Quebec) who will receive the proceeds of the insurance in the event that none of the primary beneficiaries that you have designated are living at the time of your death.

## Your right to convert to a permanent life insurance policy

At any time, up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the health of the insured person , you may convert the insurance in effect under this policy . The converted insurance will be for an amount not to exceed the Sum Insured (provided on the Policy Schedule) and will be on any permanent plan we make available for such conversion.

To exercise the conversion option, you must complete an application form which we will provide and pay us the first premium required for the converted insurance. The amount of this premium will depend on the age of the insured person at the time the conversion option is exercised, the risk classification used for this policy and the plan of the converted insurance.

The converted policy will not include any waiver of premium benefits that you may have had on this policy .

## Before we will pay any claim under this policy , the person making the claim (the claimant) must provide:

- Proof, satisfactory to us , that the insured person has died;
- Upon our request, access to any medical records that we require to assess the claim, including an attending physician's statement and a coroner's report.

In addition, the claimant must provide further proof of claim, if applicable.

In all cases, the proof must be provided within one (1) year of the date of death of the insured person and any cost incurred in providing proof of claim is at the claimant's expense.

- The insured person dies; or
- We receive request from you to cancel your coverage; or

- The end of the grace period if premiums are not paid; or
- Upon a fraudulent claim made by you or the beneficiary; or
- The insured person's 80th birthday.

We will renew this policy and insurance in effect at the end of the initial 20 year period for successive 20 year renewal periods each of the same length as the initial period, except the renewal anniversary nearest to the insured person's 80th birthday. The final renewal period will only run until the insured person's 80th birthday, at which point the policy will end and there will be no further renewal.

If a benefit is payable, we will pay the benefit to:

- Your beneficiary(ies) ; or
- If there is no beneficiary when the insured person dies, to you or your estate.

The right to name or change the beneficiary designation is reserved to you only. You do not need the consent of any beneficiary or beneficiaries to change any beneficiary under this policy , unless any rule of law requires his or her consent. All beneficiary designations are revocable unless otherwise stated or unless any contrary law applies.

If you wish to name or change your beneficiary , you must submit a written request to us , but such change shall not be binding on us until received at our Head Office. We insure our homes and cars without a second thought. But what about the family's most precious assets - ourselves, our spouses or partners, and our children? If you were to die, how would your loved ones cope financially?

By choosing TD 20-year Term Life insurance, you've taken an important step in helping to secure the financial future of those you love if you were to die. Your coverage could provide a tax-free, lump sum benefit that can: ● Help cover tuition costs to benefit your children's future ● Help pay down a mortgage so your family can remain in the family home ● Help ensure your funeral expenses won't become a burden for them at an already difficult time ● Provide cash for day-to-day living expenses ● Provide extra money to pay medical bills or outstanding debts TD 20-Year Term Life insurance is one of the simplest ways to protect your family: ● Your premiums are fixed for each 20-year term and are guaranteed not to increase during that 20-year term. To exercise the conversion option, you must complete an application form which we will provide and pay us the first premium required for the converted insurance. The amount of this premium will depend on the age of the insured person at the time the conversion option is exercised, the risk classification used for this policy and the plan of the converted insurance.

The converted policy will not include any waiver of premium benefits that you may have had on this policy .

## Before we will pay any claim under this policy , the person making the claim (the claimant) must provide:

- Proof, satisfactory to us , that the insured person has died;
- Upon our request, access to any medical records that we require to assess the claim, including an attending physician's statement and a coroner's report.

In addition, the claimant must provide further proof of claim, if applicable.

In all cases, the proof must be provided within one (1) year of the date of death of the insured person and any cost incurred in providing proof of claim is at the claimant's expense.

Making a claim SAMPLE

## When insurance coverage ends

## All coverage under this policy will end on the earliest of the date when any of the following occurs:

- The insured person dies; or
- We receive request from you to cancel your coverage; or

<!-- image -->

- The end of the grace period if premiums are not paid; or
- Upon a fraudulent claim made by you or the beneficiary; or
- The insured person's 80th birthday.

We will renew this policy and insurance in effect at the end of the initial 20 year period for successive 20 year renewal periods each of the same length as the initial period, except the renewal anniversary nearest to the insured person's 80th birthday. The final renewal period will only run until the insured person's 80th birthday, at which point the policy will end and there will be no further renewal.

If a benefit is payable, we will pay the benefit to:

- Your beneficiary(ies) ; or
- If there is no beneficiary when the insured person dies, to you or your estate.

The right to name or change the beneficiary designation is reserved to you only. You do not need the consent of any beneficiary or beneficiaries to change any beneficiary under this policy , unless any rule of law requires his or her consent. All beneficiary designations are revocable unless otherwise stated or unless any contrary law applies.

If you wish to name or change your beneficiary , you must submit a written request to us , but such change shall not be binding on us until received at our Head Office. Once the beneficiary change request has been received, it will be our responsibility to fulfill the request as of the date the request was signed, but we will not be responsible for any benefits paid to the previous beneficiary before the receipt of the beneficiary request.

Beneficiary Renewal SAMPLE

## Assignments and other documents

We are not bound by any documents that affect rights under this contract unless the document itself or written notice of it is received at our Head Office. We are not responsible for ensuring that any such document is valid or has the desired effect.

<!-- image -->

## Premium Adjustments

If incorrect information was provided during the application process that qualified the insured person for preferred rates we reserve the right to re-issue the policy with an adjusted premium

results.question: If the policyholder wishes to cancel within the 30-day review period, what happens to the premiums paid?
results.expected_answer: Any premium paid will be promptly refunded in full
results.evidence: If you decide to discontinue this policy during that period, simply contact us, provided no claim has been made, any premium paid will be promptly refunded and your policy will be cancelled as of your effective date.
results.llm_answer: Any premiums paid during the 30-day review period will be promptly refunded in full if the policy is canceled and no claim has been made.

results.question: If an irrevocable beneficiary has been designated, what must occur before a beneficiary change request is valid?
results.expected_answer: The irrevocable beneficiary must consent to the change
results.evidence: If you name someone as an irrevocable beneficiary, they must consent to certain changes you may want to make to the policy in the future. For example, an irrevocable beneficiary must consent to any request to change the beneficiary or surrender the policy.
results.llm_answer: Before a beneficiary change request is valid, the irrevocable beneficiary must consent to the change. This consent is required because the designation cannot be altered without their approval.

- Proceeds payable to a named beneficiary (someone other than 'estate') are paid directly to the beneficiary and do not flow through the estate. This means that no probate or executor fees will be deducted from, and no estate creditors can make claims against, these proceeds;

- You decide who will receive the insurance proceeds. Proceeds payable to 'Estate' are distributed, in the absence of a will, according to the intestacy laws of your province.

Contingent Beneficiary Designation: A 'secondary' list of beneficiary(ies) , (subrogated in Quebec) who will receive the proceeds of the insurance in the event that none of the primary beneficiaries that you have designated are living at the time of your death.

Irrevocable Beneficiary Designation: If you name someone as an irrevocable beneficiary , you give up the right to change the beneficiary designation, unless the irrevocable beneficiary consents. This will also affect any other desired changes you may want to make to the policy in the future. ## Contestability

We rely on the truth and completeness of the statements and answers you give us as evidence of insurability.

## General provisions

<!-- image -->

After insurance has been in effect for two (2) years from the effective date or reinstatement effective date we will treat all of the answers you gave as evidence of insurability as true, except for cases of fraudulent misrepresentation. This does not apply to information about the date of birth of the insured person in which case section Misstatement of Age and Sex at Birth above will apply.

## Waiver

We shall not be deemed to have waived or changed any condition of this policy , either in whole or in part, unless such waiver or change is clearly expressed in writing and signed by an officer of TD Life Insurance Company. Legal Action No action at law or in equity shall be brought to recover on the policy prior to the expiration of 120 days after proof of claim has been furnished in accordance with the requirements of the policy . Every action or proceeding against an insurer for the recovery of insurance money payable under the contract is absolutely barred unless commenced within the time set out in the Insurance Act (for actions or proceedings governed by the laws of Alberta and British Columbia), the Insurance Act (for actions or proceedings governed by the laws of Manitoba), the Limitations Act, 2002 (for actions or proceedings governed by the laws of Ontario), or other applicable legislation. For those actions or proceedings governed by the laws of Quebec, the prescriptive period is set out in the Civil Code of Quebec . Applicable Laws Your insurance will be governed by the laws of the province where you were resident when you initially applied for insurance under this policy , without reference to that province's rules about conflicts of laws. English Language It is the express wish of the parties that this policy and all related documents, including notices and other communications, be drawn up in the English language only. SAMPLE

## Waiver of Premiums Benefit

This section is applicable if you selected the Waiver of Premiums Benefit when you applied for TD 20-Year Term Life Insurance.

## Waiver of Premiums on total disability

If while this policy is in effect, and before the insured person's 65th birthday, the insured person becomes totally disabled , as defined below, and remains totally disabled for a continuous period of six months, we will:

- Automatically change the policy premium payment frequency to monthly, if the payment frequency is other than monthly, beginning with the date we agree to waive premiums. If after the end of the period of total disability , you wish to pay premiums other than monthly then you must notify us .
- Waive the payment of monthly premiums from the date the insured person becomes totally disabled and for as long as the total disability continues, up to the insured person's 80th birthday.

'Total disability' or 'totally disabled' shall mean that the insured person , as a result of bodily injury or disease, is wholly prevented during the first two years after the injury or the onset of the disease from performing the substantial duties of their own occupation; after the first two years the insured person must be prevented by the injury or disease, from engaging in any gainful occupation for which they are or may reasonably become qualified by training, education or experience.

results.evidence: If the insured person dies while this policy is in effect, the insurer will pay the Sum Insured to the beneficiary or your estate if no beneficiary is named.
results.llm_answer: The insurer will pay the death benefit, which is the Sum Insured minus any outstanding premiums, to the designated beneficiary(ies). If no beneficiary is named, the benefit will be paid to the policy owner or the policy owner's estate.

results.question: What are all the conditions that must be met to reinstate a lapsed policy?
results.expected_answer: The insured person must be alive; all unpaid premiums from the lapse date to the reinstatement effective date must be paid; a completed Reinstatement Application must be provided; and new evidence of insurability must be provided that TD considers satisfactory
results.evidence: In order to reinstate your policy in that time period, you must meet all of the following criteria: The insured person must be alive; You must pay us all unpaid premiums due from the lapse date up to and including the reinstatement effective date; You must provide us with a completed Reinstatement Application; and You must provide us with new evidence of insurability for the insured person that we consider satisfactory.
results.llm_answer: To reinstate a lapsed policy, the insured person must be alive, all unpaid premiums from the lapse date to the reinstatement effective date must be paid, a completed reinstatement application must be submitted, and new evidence of insurability must be provided and deemed satisfactory by the insurer.

results.expected_answer: TD will pay the policy owner 100% of premiums paid since the effective date, or since the most recent reinstatement effective date if the policy has been reinstated
results.evidence: If no insurance benefit is payable as a result of suicide, then we will pay the policy owner 100% of premiums paid since the effective date or since the most recent reinstatement effective date if the policy has been reinstated.

results.question: Under what conditions will all coverage under this policy end?
results.expected_answer: Coverage ends when the insured person dies; when TD receives a cancellation request; when premiums are not paid by the end of the grace period; upon a fraudulent claim; or on the insured person's 80th birthday
results.evidence: All coverage under this policy will end on the earliest of the date when any of the following occurs: The insured person dies; or We receive request from you to cancel your coverage; or The end of the grace period if premiums are not paid; or Upon a fraudulent claim made by you or the beneficiary; or The insured person's 80th birthday.
results.llm_answer: All coverage under this policy will end on the earliest of: the insured person's death, a request to cancel coverage, the end of the grace period if premiums are not paid, a fraudulent claim made by the policyholder or beneficiary, or the insured person's 80th birthday.

results.question: For total disability in the first two years after the onset of disease, what is the standard for disability, and how does this differ after two years?
results.expected_answer: In the first two years, the insured person must be wholly prevented from performing the substantial duties of their own occupation. After two years, the insured person must be prevented from engaging in any gainful occupation for which they are or may reasonably become qualified by training, education, or experience
results.evidence: 'Total disability' or 'totally disabled' shall mean that the insured person, as a result of bodily injury or disease, is wholly prevented during the first two years after the injury or the onset of the disease from performing the substantial duties of their own occupation; after the first two years the insured person must be prevented by the injury or disease, from engaging in any gainful occupation for which they are or may reasonably become qualified by training, education or experience.
results.llm_answer: In the first two years after the onset of disease, total disability means the insured person is wholly prevented from performing the substantial duties of their own occupation. After two years, total disability means the insured person is prevented from engaging in any gainful occupation for which they are or may reasonably become qualified by training, education, or experience.

results.question: What must a claimant provide before TD will pay a death benefit, and what is the deadline for providing proof?
results.expected_answer: The claimant must provide proof that the insured person has died and, upon TD's request, access to any required medical records including a physician's statement and coroner's report. The proof must be provided within one year of the date of death.
results.evidence: Before we will pay any claim under this policy, the person making the claim (the claimant) must provide: Proof, satisfactory to us, that the insured person has died; Upon our request, access to any medical records that we require to assess the claim, including an attending physician's statement and a coroner's report. In all cases, the proof must be provided within one (1) year of the date of death of the insured person
results.llm_answer: The claimant must provide proof of death and, if requested, medical records including an attending physician's statement and a coroner's report. Proof must be provided within one year of the insured person's death.

results.question: What are the eligibility requirements a proposed insured person must meet at the time of application?
results.expected_answer: The proposed insured person must be a Canadian citizen, or have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident status by the Canadian Government, and must be at least 18 years old and within 6 months of their 60th birthday
results.evidence: To be eligible to apply for insurance coverage under this policy, a proposed insured person must, at the time of application: Be a Canadian citizen; or Have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government; and Be at least 18 years old and within 6 months of the 60th birthday.
results.llm_answer: A proposed insured person must be a Canadian citizen or have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident status by the Canadian Government, be at least 18 years old, and be within 6 months of their 60th birthday at the time of application.

results.question: Under what conditions will the Waiver of Premiums benefit not apply even if the insured person is totally disabled?
results.expected_answer: The waiver will not apply if total disability results from: attempted suicide or self-inflicted injury; war or military service; commission of a criminal act; an accident while operating a vehicle over the legal blood alcohol limit; or taking a drug other than as prescribed by a licensed physician
results.evidence: We will not waive premiums if total disability results, either directly or indirectly, from one or more of the following causes: Attempted suicide or self-inflicted injury...; War, whether declared or undeclared...; The commission or attempted commission by the insured person of a criminal act; An accident that occurs while the insured person is operating any kind of conveyance while their blood alcohol level exceeds the legal limit...; Taking a drug in a manner other than prescribed by a licensed physician.
results.llm_answer: The Waiver of Premiums benefit will not apply if total disability results from excluded events, if the insured person converts the policy while totally disabled, or if the notice of total disability is given more than 12 months after the premiums were due.

results.question: What conditions govern the notice and proof requirements for total disability claims?
results.expected_answer: TD must receive notice of total disability while the insured person is alive and continues to be totally disabled; proof must be received within 3 months of when notice was given; TD will not waive premiums falling due more than 12 months before the insured person gives notice
results.evidence: We must receive notice of total disability while the insured person is alive and continues to be totally disabled. We must also receive proof of the total disability of the insured person within 3 months of the date notice was provided to us. We will not waive any premiums falling due more than 12 months before the insured person gives us notice of total disability.
results.llm_answer: Notice of total disability must be received while the insured is alive and disabled, and proof of total disability must be submitted within 3 months of the notice.

## Waiver of Premiums on total disability

If while this policy is in effect, and before the insured person's 65th birthday, the insured person becomes totally disabled , as defined below, and remains totally disabled for a continuous period of six months, we will:

- Automatically change the policy premium payment frequency to monthly, if the payment frequency is other than monthly, beginning with the date we agree to waive premiums. If after the end of the period of total disability , you wish to pay premiums other than monthly then you must notify us .

## Your right to convert to a permanent life insurance policy

At any time, up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the health of the insured person , you may convert the insurance in effect under this policy . The converted insurance will be for an amount not to exceed the Sum Insured (provided on the Policy Schedule) and will be on any permanent plan we make available for such conversion.

To exercise the conversion option, you must complete an application form which we will provide and pay us the first premium required for the converted insurance. The amount of this premium will depend on the age of the insured person at the time the conversion option is exercised, the risk classification used for this policy and the plan of the converted insurance.

The converted policy will not include any waiver of premium benefits that you may have had on this policy .

## Before we will pay any claim under this policy , the person making the claim (the claimant) must provide:

- Proof, satisfactory to us , that the insured person has died;
- Upon our request, access to any medical records that we require to assess the claim, including an attending physician's statement and a coroner's report.

In addition, the claimant must provide further proof of claim, if applicable.

In all cases, the proof must be provided within one (1) year of the date of death of the insured person and any cost incurred in providing proof of claim is at the claimant's expense.

At any time, up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the health of the insured person , you may convert the insurance in effect under this policy . The converted insurance will be for an amount not to exceed the Sum Insured (provided on the Policy Schedule) and will be on any permanent plan we make available for such conversion.

To exercise the conversion option, you must complete an application form which we will provide and pay us the first premium required for the converted insurance. The amount of this premium will depend on the age of the insured person at the time the conversion option is exercised, the risk classification used for this policy and the plan of the converted insurance.

The converted policy will not include any waiver of premium benefits that you may have had on this policy .

## Before we will pay any claim under this policy , the person making the claim (the claimant) must provide:

- Proof, satisfactory to us , that the insured person has died;
- Upon our request, access to any medical records that we require to assess the claim, including an attending physician's statement and a coroner's report.

## Your right to convert to a permanent life insurance policy

At any time, up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the health of the insured person , you may convert the insurance in effect under this policy . The converted insurance will be for an amount not to exceed the Sum Insured (provided on the Policy Schedule) and will be on any permanent plan we make available for such conversion.

To exercise the conversion option, you must complete an application form which we will provide and pay us the first premium required for the converted insurance. The amount of this premium will depend on the age of the insured person at the time the conversion option is exercised, the risk classification used for this policy and the plan of the converted insurance.

The converted policy will not include any waiver of premium benefits that you may have had on this policy .

## If my health changes during the term of my coverage, will my premiums increase?

Your premium is set and guaranteed for each 20-year term of your insurance coverage. It will not change during each 20-year term, regardless of changes in your age or health (provided premium payments are made when due and the policy does not lapse ).

Yes, you can convert to a permanent life insurance policy , with no medical questions, at any time up to and including the policy anniversary nearest the insured's 69th birthday. - Proceeds payable to a named beneficiary (someone other than 'estate') are paid directly to the beneficiary and do not flow through the estate. This means that no probate or executor fees will be deducted from, and no estate creditors can make claims against, these proceeds;
- Proceeds are available to the beneficiary as soon as the claim is approved since they do not become part of the estate. Settlement of the estate usually takes a few months but can take years depending on the circumstances;
- You decide who will receive the insurance proceeds. Proceeds payable to 'Estate' are distributed, in the absence of a will, according to the intestacy laws of your province.

Contingent Beneficiary Designation: A 'secondary' list of beneficiary(ies) , (subrogated in Quebec) who will receive the proceeds of the insurance in the event that none of the primary beneficiaries that you have designated are living at the time of your death.

Irrevocable Beneficiary Designation: If you name someone as an irrevocable beneficiary , you give up the right to change the beneficiary designation, unless the irrevocable beneficiary consents. This will also affect any other desired changes you may want to make to the policy in the future. In Quebec your spouse is automatically deemed to be an irrevocable beneficiary unless specifically designated as revocable.

Example - An irrevocable beneficiary must consent to any request to change the beneficiary or surrender the policy.

Minor: A person who has not attained the age of majority and, thus, has limited contractual capacity.

Primary Beneficiary Designation: A list of beneficiary(ies) , who will receive the proceeds of the insurance in the event of your death.

Should you choose to designate a trustee for minor children refer to page 2 of the form and indicate the First, Middle and Last Name, Date of Birth or Age, Percent of Benefit to be paid in the event of your passing, and if the proceeds will be Revocable or Irrevocable for each individual(s) that you wish to name as beneficiary(ies) ;

<!-- image -->

## Section 2

- Sign and date the form (signature line 1);
- If in the past you designated an irrevocable beneficiary(ies) , please also have them sign this form (signature line 2);

● Should the Owner of this coverage be a corporation we will require a corporate seal to accompany the signature of the signing officer. If a corporate seal is not available we will accept the signatures of 2 signing officers with their titles. (signature lines 3&4); ● Please have this form witnessed by someone who is not related to you and who is also not named as a beneficiary . (signature line 5). Step 2 ● Mail the 'Request for Change of Beneficiary ' to TD Life in the enclosed self-addressed return envelope. TD Life will validate and record your Change of Beneficiary and return a confirmation letter to you for your records. Note: TD Life cannot warrant the legal effectiveness of any change of beneficiary . ● Beneficiaries can be designated as Revocable or Irrevocable. If you name someone as an irrevocable beneficiary , they must consent to certain changes you may want to make to the policy in the future. For example, an irrevocable beneficiary must consent to any request to change the beneficiary or surrender the policy . In Quebec your spouse is automatically deemed to be an irrevocable beneficiary unless specifically designated as revocable; Points for Consideration SAMPLE

- To change an irrevocable minor beneficiary designation in the future, the minor child must have reached the age of majority

## Your right to convert to a permanent life insurance policy

At any time, up to and including the policy anniversary nearest to the insured person's 69th birthday, regardless of the health of the insured person , you may convert the insurance in effect under this policy . The converted insurance will be for an amount not to exceed the Sum Insured (provided on the Policy Schedule) and will be on any permanent plan we make available for such conversion.

To exercise the conversion option, you must complete an application form which we will provide and pay us the first premium required for the converted insurance. ## TD 20-Year Term Life insurance-the smart choice

We insure our homes and cars without a second thought. But what about the family's most precious assets - ourselves, our spouses or partners, and our children? If you were to die, how would your loved ones cope financially?

By choosing TD 20-year Term Life insurance, you've taken an important step in helping to secure the financial future of those you love if you were to die. Your coverage could provide a tax-free, lump sum benefit that can: ● Help cover tuition costs to benefit your children's future ● Help pay down a mortgage so your family can remain in the family home ● Help ensure your funeral expenses won't become a burden for them at an already difficult time ● Provide cash for day-to-day living expenses ● Provide extra money to pay medical bills or outstanding debts TD 20-Year Term Life insurance is one of the simplest ways to protect your family: ● Your premiums are fixed for each 20-year term and are guaranteed not to increase during that 20-year term. By choosing TD 20-year Term Life insurance, you've taken an important step in helping to secure the financial future of those you love if you were to die. By choosing TD 20-year Term Life insurance, you've taken an important step in helping to secure the financial future of those you love if you were to die. Contingent Beneficiary Designation: A 'secondary' list of beneficiary(ies) , (subrogated in Quebec) who will receive the proceeds of the insurance in the event that none of the primary beneficiaries that you have designated are living at the time of your death.

Contingent Beneficiary Designation: A 'secondary' list of beneficiary(ies) , (subrogated in Quebec) who will receive the proceeds of the insurance in the event that none of the primary beneficiaries that you have designated are living at the time of your death.

Minor: A person who has not attained the age of majority and, thus, has limited contractual capacity.

We insure our homes and cars without a second thought. But what about the family's most precious assets - ourselves, our spouses or partners, and our children? If you were to die, how would your loved ones cope financially?

By choosing TD 20-year Term Life insurance, you've taken an important step in helping to secure the financial future of those you love if you were to die. Your coverage could provide a tax-free, lump sum benefit that can: ● Help cover tuition costs to benefit your children's future ● Help pay down a mortgage so your family can remain in the family home ● Help ensure your funeral expenses won't become a burden for them at an already difficult time ● Provide cash for day-to-day living expenses ● Provide extra money to pay medical bills or outstanding debts TD 20-Year Term Life insurance is one of the simplest ways to protect your family: ● Your premiums are fixed for each 20-year term and are guaranteed not to increase during that 20-year term. We insure our homes and cars without a second thought. But what about the family's most precious assets - ourselves, our spouses or partners, and our children? If you were to die, how would your loved ones cope financially?

We insure our homes and cars without a second thought. But what about the family's most precious assets - ourselves, our spouses or partners, and our children? If you were to die, how would your loved ones cope financially?

Lapse refers to the termination of this policy because the premium was not paid within the grace period .

Lapse Date refers to the date the policy lapses .

Insured person is the person whose life is insured under this policy .

Policy means this document which provides evidence of your insurance.

Policy Owner is the person or party who owns this individual insurance policy . The policy owner is not necessarily the person whose life is insured.

<!-- image -->

Reinstatement is the restoration of a lapsed policy as described in the section, 'Putting your policy back into effect'.

Reinstatement Effective Date is the date this policy is reinstated as described in the section, 'Putting your policy back into effect'.

Term Insurance is a type of insurance that provides protection for a limited number of years.

To be eligible to apply for insurance coverage under this policy , a proposed insured person must, at the time of application:

- Be a Canadian citizen; or
- Have applied for or been granted Permanent Resident (Landed Immigrant) status by the Canadian Government; and
- Be at least 18 years old and within 6 months of the 60th birthday.

If a death benefit is payable under this policy , then we will pay the Sum Insured in effect at the time of death minus any outstanding premiums that are owed at the time the insured person dies.

This policy ends on the date the insured person dies.

Eligibility How the death benefit is calculated SAMPLE

## Living Benefit

While this policy is active, you may request an advance payment of 50% of the Death Benefit if the insured person has a terminal illness (to a maximum of $100,000). The payment of this Living benefit is subject to our administrative rules in effect at the time of your request and subject to the following conditions:

- You must be diagnosed with a terminal illness with a life expectancy of 12 months or less; and

<!-- image -->

- Your policy must be in force and paid current.
- We will pay the benefit to the insured person;
- Any irrevocable beneficiary or policy owner under this policy must consent to the payment of the benefit;
- A special collateral assignment arrangement is used to assign the policy to us when the benefit is approved and paid. By administering the benefit as a loan means that in most instances the benefit is non-taxable.

When you claim the Living benefit, you agree to the following conditions and limitations on your rights as a policy owner :

- You may not cancel this policy;
- If premiums are not paid, either directly or through the waiver benefit, the amount of any unpaid premiums will increase the amount of the living benefit.  The living benefit amount and any unpaid premium amount will accumulate interest until the death of the insured person . Contingent Beneficiary Designation: A 'secondary' list of beneficiary(ies) , (subrogated in Quebec) who will receive the proceeds of the insurance in the event that none of the primary beneficiaries that you have designated are living at the time of your death.

We insure our homes and cars without a second thought. But what about the family's most precious assets - ourselves, our spouses or partners, and our children? If you were to die, how would your loved ones cope financially?

By choosing TD 20-year Term Life insurance, you've taken an important step in helping to secure the financial future of those you love if you were to die. Your coverage could provide a tax-free, lump sum benefit that can: ● Help cover tuition costs to benefit your children's future ● Help pay down a mortgage so your family can remain in the family home ● Help ensure your funeral expenses won't become a burden for them at an already difficult time ● Provide cash for day-to-day living expenses ● Provide extra money to pay medical bills or outstanding debts TD 20-Year Term Life insurance is one of the simplest ways to protect your family: ● Your premiums are fixed for each 20-year term and are guaranteed not to increase during that 20-year term. As the owner of this insurance coverage, you are the only person entitled to change the beneficiary , whether the coverage is for yourself or for your entire family. You must, however, obtain consent of any previously designated irrevocable beneficiaries.

## Form Do's and Don'ts

- Type or print all information on the forms enclosed, using a ball point pen;
- Do not use correction fluid (liquid paper);
- Initial any corrections/changes;
- Use of all lines is not required, if necessary you can use a separate piece of paper to list all of your beneficiary designations.

## Section 1

- Under Primary Beneficiary (see definition below), indicate the First, Middle and Last Name, Date of Birth or Age, Percent of Benefit to be paid in the event of your death, and if the proceeds will be Revocable or Irrevocable for each individual(s) that you wish to name as beneficiary(ies) ;
